chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, who said: He narrated to me, Abu Ali al-Wasiti, from Abdullah ibn Ismat, from Yahya ibn Abdullah, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) entered his house, and he found Aisha facing Fatimah, shouting at her, while she was saying: 'By God, O daughter of Khadijah, you do not think that your mother has superiority over us. What superiority did she have over us? She was nothing but like one of us.' Fatimah heard her statement, and when Fatimah saw the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), she cried. He said to her: 'What is making you cry, O daughter of Muhammad?' She replied: 'I remembered my mother and she slighted her, so I cried.' The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) became angry, then said: 'Be quiet, O Humayra (Aisha). Indeed, God, the Blessed and Exalted, has blessed the fertile and affectionate woman. And indeed, Khadijah (may God have mercy on her) bore from me a pure one, who is Abdullah and he is al-Mutahhar, and she bore from me al-Qasim, and Fatimah, and Ruqayyah, and Umm Kulthum, and Zaynab. And you are one whom God made barren, so you did not bear anything for me.'

ai.seo_question: What was the Prophet's response to Aisha's criticism of Khadijah regarding her status among the wives?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) rebukes Aisha for diminishing Khadijah’s status, emphasizing that Khadijah was the mother of all his progeny, including the four daughters and the sons Abdullah and Al-Qasim. Notably, the text highlights Aisha’s barrenness as a contrast to Khadijah’s fertility, a point of significance in Shia scholarship to underscore Khadijah’s unique role as the primary mother of the Prophet’s lineage. This incident serves as a foundational argument for the superiority of Khadijah among the wives, linking her maternal contribution directly to the continuation of the Prophet’s bloodline.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-117 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of Abu Ali al-Vaseti, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ismat, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Amr ibn Abil Miqdam, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “

Once when God’s Prophet (MGB) entered his house, he (MGB) heard that Ayesha was yelling at Fatimah (MGB). She was saying, ‘O Khadijah’s daughter! I swear by God that you believe that your mother was better than us. What was in her that made her nobler than us?’ Fatimah who was listening to her cried when she saw the Prophet (MGB). The Prophet (MGB) looked at her and asked, ‘O daughter of Muhammad! Why are you crying?’ She replied, ‘Ayesha mentioned my mother’s name with disrespect and I cried.’ The Prophet of God (MGB) became angry, turned to Ayesha and said, ‘O Homeyra! Be silent. The Blessed the Sublime God has honored kind women who give birth to children. Khadijah - may God may have mercy upon her - has brought two sons from me. The first one is called Tahir, Abdullah or Mutah’har. The second one is called Qasim. Khadijah has delivered four daughters for me who are Fatimah (MGB), Ruqayah, Umm Kulthum and Zaynab. However, you are one whom God has made barren and have not given birth to any child for me.”
